author: WP14
summary: Audio chapter: selection axis, SDL3 and ALSA mixers, SoundEffect and 3D formulas, dynamic streaming, XACT objects, XNB formats, corrections history, open limits, microphone and evidence. Mostly current; stale points are the SDL_INIT_AUDIO pin (now per-stream), XNB decoding route (now CNA's own decoder), RendererDetails, wave-bank streaming, SoundBank disposal and the microphone BufferDuration defect (fixed). Audio engine internals and the guide already held the mixer and device material; two new deep dives carry the caller semantics, XACT runtime and evidence.

sections.heading: Audio implementation is a separate axis

concepts.text: CNA parses XACT containers with its own parser (XactParser) and plays the result through the selected mixer.
tokens: XACT is a real parser and player

concepts.text: The default audio implementation plays through SDL3_mixer, while the native ALSA route uses CNA's own mixer.
Audio is an independent build axis rather than a property of the window/input platform.
CNA uses neither Microsoft's XACT engine nor FNA's FAudio.
tokens: it does not use Microsoft's XACT engine or FNA's FAudio

concepts.text: The design yields usable sound effects, streaming, capture and much of the XACT object model on the mixer-backed selections.
It also defines the limits: no auxiliary reverb bus, no native 3D graph, and one per-track cooked-callback slot shared by filtering and stereo crossfeed.

concepts.text: Under SDL3 audio the process-wide mixer requests signed 16-bit stereo at 44.1 kHz and uses the format the device negotiates.
concepts.note: At TARGET the mixer is memory-backed (MIX_CreateMixer) and fed by the selected IAudioDevice.

concepts.text: Decoded MIX_Audio objects hold assets and each playback uses a MIX_Track for gain, rate, looping and the cooked callback.
SoundEffect owns decoded audio while SoundEffectInstance controls a track.

concepts.note: Per-stream reference replaces a permanent pin.

concepts.text: A generation counter rejects stale tracks after DestroyMixer().
Production code never calls DestroyMixer(), so mixer lifetime is effectively process lifetime.
CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=ALSA is the Linux SDL-free playback and capture route.
The ALSA device implements the same IAudioDevice contract as SDL3, SDL2 and NULL; the XNA classes call a common mixer facade.
ALSA headers are needed at build time while libasound.so.2 is loaded at run time; a missing library or device becomes NoAudioHardwareException rather than preventing startup.
tokens: a machine without ALSA still starts the program

concepts.text: The ALSA backend opens default or CNA_AUDIO_DEVICE, requests float stereo at 44.1 kHz, negotiates the real format and writes about 10 ms periods from one device thread.
tokens: aims for a period of about 10 ms

concepts.text: Underrun and suspend recovery plus a bounded 100 ms wait keep Stop responsive.
tokens: On EAGAIN it waits up to 100 ms

concepts.text: ALSA null and file devices have no clock, so CNA paces them in real time.
CNA's mixer converts each track to the negotiated rate at its pitch ratio, applies gain, runs the per-track callback used by filters and pan, then adds it at master gain.
Mono duplicates to stereo and streams wait silently for more queued data instead of terminating.
The ALSA mixer's linear resampler matches the FAudio/FNA choice but can sound different from SDL3's resampler.
concepts.note: The perceptual difference from SDL3 is not measured by any test.

concepts.text: ALSA capture enumerates capture PCMs, opens plughw or an explicit CNA_AUDIO_RECORDING_DEVICE and reads 10 ms blocks into a bounded eight-second queue on a capture thread.
ALSA tests use null and file devices with known bytes; real microphones, PipeWire/PulseAudio/sound-card playback, latency and multichannel devices are not attempted.

concepts.text: 3D pan projects the displacement onto Forward x Up (the listener's right axis), not world X.

concepts.note: DopplerScale enters inside the Doppler factor (emitter times global scale), and the rate is floored at 0.01.
